Subject: Confidentiality Schedule — Donor Letters Pilot

We have reviewed your draft schedule. Four items require adjustment before we can move to signature.

**1. External color specialist (first batch).**
We engage an external color specialist only for the first batch. We ask that the “subcontractors may process materials” clause be amended to expressly permit a single named third-party color consultant. That consultant must:
- sign a confidentiality agreement containing terms at least as restrictive as ours;
- receive only redacted or non-textual calibration data (color targets, ICC referrals, or the physical scanner target sheet); and
- confirm deletion of all delivered data once the calibration profile is finalized.

If you prefer no external eyes on the files at all, our fallback is that your team run the first batch through your reference scanner and send us the resulting calibration profile plus a set of synthetic resolution targets. That preserves the calibration workflow without a subcontractor.

**2. Calibration access — master images vs. crops.**
Cropped files degrade color-ringing and texture information that the specialist needs to build an accurate input profile. For the pilot we require temporary access to the master image files for the first batch (or, at minimum, the first 20 folios plus every frame containing a color target). If you will not release masters, acceptable alternatives are:
- **(a)** we supply the scanner’s calibration target; you capture it with your own devices and transmit only the measured color values and ICC profile; or
- **(b)** we receive lossless RAW/linear TIFF frames for the first batch only, with all text regions cropped out and no derivative crops.

**3. Correction window and backup rotation.**
We need ten business days from initial delivery to identify and remediate scan defects (geometry, tone, crop). During this window, working copies may reside on our production SAN. Our backup rotation overwrites older snapshots on a rolling 45-day cycle; any donor-letter files contained in a backup will therefore be cryptographically erased or overwritten by the rotation following day 45. We propose this be codified as the outer retention limit.

**4. Publicity carve-out.**
The blanket written-consent requirement for publicity is too broad. We request a categorical carve-out for an “anonymized process image” defined as a photograph showing only equipment, workstations, or blurred foreground hardware with **no legible letter text, no donor names, and no metadata**. We would prefer that you pre-approve one such image in writing before release.

**Proposed access and deletion schedule**
- **Day 0:** Secure transfer of batch files to our workspaces.
- **Day 0–2:** Extraction of calibration data for the external specialist; specialist deletes all materials within 3 days of profile issuance.
- **Day 0–10:** Correction window. Defect log submitted by 5:00 local time on day 10.
- **Day 11:** Corrected files returned to you. Active working copies on our servers deleted within 48 hours of your written acceptance.
- **Day 46–90:** Next rotational backup overwrites any residual copies; digital-deletion certificate issued within 5 business days after rotation.

If the master-image access remains the sticking point, we can shorten the correction window to 7 days for the pilot and accept pre-publication approval of the anonymized process image, provided the calibration alternative in §2 is accepted.

We await your redline.

**Subject: Donor letters pilot — proposed schedule for signature**

We can accept the seven-day correction window and calibration alternative (a), with the following terms in the signed schedule.

1. **Calibration and access.** The studio supplies its scanner target. The Archive captures the target on its reference scanner and provides the measured values and ICC profile. We can also supply a physical calibration sheet. Two collections will be scanned and checked by Archive staff only. The Archive will identify them by collection code before transfer and retain their originals, masters and derivatives.

2. **First-batch specialist.** Replace the general subcontractor permission with approval for one color specialist, named in the schedule and bound in writing to equivalent confidentiality terms before access. The specialist may receive target data and the calibration sheet. If those prove insufficient, the studio may identify the defect and request a lossless, full-frame masked image from another collection. The Archive must prepare and approve each image before release, permanently masking handwriting and identifying details and removing identifying metadata. The specialist must delete all digital inputs within three calendar days of profile issuance, subject to the deletion deadline below, and confirm deletion in writing.

3. **Correction and deletion.** For each studio-scanned batch, Day 0 is initial delivery of scans to the Archive. The studio may keep working copies on its production SAN through Day 7 for corrections, with the defect log due that day and corrected files due on Day 8. Delete all studio and specialist copies of donor material, including temporary files and masked images, by the end of Day 10. All days are calendar days. Written acceptance does not extend that deadline. Exclude pilot files from snapshots and backups from intake onward. Within five business days after deletion, provide a certificate identifying the batch, systems covered and deletion dates, together with the specialist’s confirmation.

4. **Incident contact.** Before signature, each party will enter its incident lead’s name, monitored email and telephone number. The studio must notify the Archive lead promptly and within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, including at the specialist. The first notice should identify the affected batches and containment steps known at the time.

5. **Publicity.** The Archive may approve one equipment-only photograph in writing for a specified use. Submit the exact final image, stripped of metadata, with its caption and proposed outlet. Keep donor materials, screens displaying files, labels and identifying reflections out of frame. Approval applies only to that image and use.

**Outstanding exception.** Please confirm that the production SAN can exclude pilot files from snapshots before intake. If it cannot, identify the affected system and the earliest guaranteed erasure date so we can decide whether to use a separate workspace. A 45–90-day backup tail is outside the Archive’s proposed terms.

Subject: RE: Donor letters pilot — proposed schedule for signature

We can proceed on the terms below, with two adjustments.

**1. Correction window and deletion deadline.**  
We accept the Day 7 defect-log milestone. However, we need ten calendar days to complete corrections; a seven-day cycle does not allow for re-scanning, tone correction, and quality verification of the full set. We propose:

- **Day 0:** initial delivery of scans to the Archive.  
- **Day 7:** defect log due to the Archive.  
- **Day 10:** corrected files delivered to the Archive.  
- **Day 12:** deletion of all studio and specialist copies, including temporary files and masked images.

Because the pilot files will reside in the segregated workspace described below, extending the deletion deadline to Day 12 does not create the residual-copy risk you are trying to eliminate. Written acceptance on Day 10 will not extend the deletion deadline.

**2. Backup segregation and SAN confirmation.**  
The production SAN cannot exclude individual files or folders from its snapshot schedule before intake; once written, the next scheduled snapshot captures the file, and that snapshot rotates out on a 45-day cycle. We therefore propose that the pilot be ingested directly into a segregated, non-snapshotted workspace that sits outside the production SAN backup policy. That workspace will be provisioned before intake, will carry no snapshots, and will be decommissioned and wiped on Day 12. This guarantees that no donor-letter file enters the 45-day rotation.

If you prefer to avoid any transfer into our production environment, we can work from an air-gapped terminal and an encrypted local drive, with the same Day 12 wipe and a certificate covering the drive, the terminal’s boot volume, and the specialist’s endpoint. If neither segregated workspace is acceptable, the affected system is the production SAN, and the earliest guaranteed erasure date for any residual snapshot copy is Day 45 from intake.

**3. Terms accepted without change.**  
- **Calibration alternative (a):** the Archive supplies the scanner target and physical calibration sheet; we use the measured values and ICC profile.  
- **Specialist:** one named color specialist, bound in writing before access, limited to target data and Archive-approved masked images, deleting all digital inputs within three calendar days of profile issuance.  
- **Publicity:** one equipment-only photograph, pre-approved with final image, caption, outlet, and metadata stripped.  
- **Incident contact:** names and monitored contacts exchanged before signature; notice within 24 hours.

Please confirm whether the segregated workspace or the air-gapped terminal model works for your side. If so, we will send the final schedule for signature.

The Archive accepts the segregated workspace and the Day 12 deletion deadline. Please circulate the signature copy with the following terms.

Provision the workspace before intake and route pilot files directly into it. Keep donor material, including temporary files and specialist inputs, out of snapshots and backups from intake through deletion. For each batch, Day 0 is initial delivery to the Archive. The defect log is due on Day 7 and corrected files on Day 10. Wipe and decommission the batch workspace and delete all studio and specialist copies by the end of Day 12, regardless of when the Archive accepts delivery. These are calendar days. Within five business days after deletion, provide a certificate identifying the batch, systems covered and deletion dates, together with the specialist’s written confirmation.

Please correct one detail in the calibration clause. **The studio supplies its scanner target.** The Archive captures that target on its reference scanner and supplies the measured values and ICC profile. We can also provide a physical calibration sheet. The two collections identified by code remain exclusively with Archive staff for scanning and quality checks.

For the first batch only, the named specialist may receive calibration data under the agreed written confidentiality terms. If those data prove insufficient, the studio may identify the defect and request a masked image from another collection. The Archive will prepare and approve each such image before release, permanently masking handwriting and identifying content and removing identifying metadata. The specialist must delete all digital inputs by the earlier of three calendar days after profile issuance or Day 12.

Please include each party’s incident lead, monitored email and telephone number before signature. The studio must notify the Archive promptly and within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, including at the specialist. Publication of one equipment-only photograph requires the Archive’s prior written approval of the exact metadata-stripped image, caption and outlet. Approval applies only to that use.

The segregated workspace resolves the backup exception. The only remaining drafting correction is the scanner-target assignment above.

**Subject:** RE: Donor letters pilot — signature copy

We accept the corrected calibration clause: **the studio supplies its scanner target**, the Archive captures it on its reference scanner and supplies the measured values and ICC profile, and the Archive may also provide a physical calibration sheet. The two collections identified by code remain exclusively with Archive staff for scanning and quality checks. No further drafting corrections on that point.

All remaining terms are accepted as written:

- Segregated workspace provisioned before intake; pilot files routed directly into it; donor material, temporary files, and specialist inputs kept out of snapshots and backups from intake through deletion.
- Day 0 initial delivery to the Archive; defect log due Day 7; corrected files due Day 10; workspace wiped and all studio and specialist copies deleted by end of Day 12, calendar days, regardless of acceptance.
- Deletion certificate within five business days after deletion, identifying batch, systems covered, and deletion dates, together with the specialist’s written confirmation.
- First-batch specialist limited to calibration data and Archive-approved masked images; deletion of all digital inputs by the earlier of three calendar days after profile issuance or Day 12.

Before signature, we will insert our incident lead’s name, monitored email and telephone number into the schedule, and we ask you to insert yours. The studio will notify the Archive promptly and within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, including at the specialist.

For publicity, we will submit the exact final image, stripped of metadata, with its caption and proposed outlet for the Archive’s prior written approval; approval applies only to that use.

No further drafting corrections on our side. We can circulate the signature copy for execution.
Please circulate the signature copy. The Archive will enter its incident lead’s name, monitored email and telephone number before signing. We have no outstanding exceptions.
